newsitem.title: UK: Med, Mideast tanker rates steady, quiet.
newsitem.headline: Med, Mideast tanker rates steady, quiet.

text.p: Mediterranean 80,000 tonne crude tanker rates held firm in quiet activity on Tuesday after a spectacular rise last week.
Brokers said few if any fixtures had been reported for Med 80,000 tonne vessels, but notionally rates still looked firm at around W150, up some 50 points from 10 days ago.
"Hardly anything has been fixed today...but I don't see it going down for the moment," an Italian broker said, adding that the market was looking particularly strong for prompt fixtures.
Med 130,000 tonne ships were little changed at around W90-95, steady over the past week.
The Middle East market was also reported stable but quiet, with very large crude carriers (VLCCs) to Japan assessed at around W65 and to Europe and Singapore at W55.
One broker said Kuwait Petroleum Corp was in the market for an ultra-large crude carrier (ULCC) to the U.S. Gulf at about W45 for 400,000-450,000 tonnes.
Transatlantic rates were steady with North Sea/USAC VLCCs at W62.5 and million barrel cargoes at around W95. West Africa/USG rates were likewise unchanged at similar levels to North Sea/USAC.
In the inter-U.K./Cont sector, 80,000 tonne vessels continued to be fixed at around W115-120.
One broker said rates for 130,000 tonne ships in this sector, currently at around W100, could rise with a shortage of vessels for early Feb.

"It might look as if there are enough ships (in early Feb) but not all of them are workable, with Statoil approval needed for ships into Mongstad and other berthing restrictions...We could see a jump," he added.
